## 💻 Essential R Commands for Regression

```r
# Fit standard Ordinary Least Squares model
model <- lm(Y ~ X1 + X2 + X3, data = my_data)

# Parameter estimates, standard errors, t-statistics, R-squared
summary(model)

# ANOVA decomposition and Extra Sum of Squares F-test
anova(reduced_model, full_model)

# Confidence intervals for beta parameters
confint(model, level = 0.95)

# Fitted values and residuals
y_hat <- fitted(model)
resids <- residuals(model)

# Diagnostics: Leverage (hat values) and Cook's distance
hii <- hatvalues(model)
cooks <- cooks.distance(model)
dffits_val <- dffits(model)
vif_vals <- car::vif(model)
```

---

## 📊 Standard 4-Panel Diagnostic Plots
```r
par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
plot(model)
```
1. **Residuals vs Fitted:** Tests linearity and homoskedasticity.
2. **Normal Q-Q Plot:** Tests normality of errors $\varepsilon_i \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma^2)$.
3. **Scale-Location:** Evaluates constant variance across fitted range.
4. **Residuals vs Leverage:** Identifies influential observations ($D_i > 0.5$).
